newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria postpones ruling on Balkanbank insolvency.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria postpones ruling on Balkanbank insolvency.

text.p: A Bulgarian court on Monday postponed ruling on an insolvency case against state-owned Balkanbank for June because a report on its financial state has not been submitted in due time, a court official said.

"The Sofia City Court postponed the ruling until June because financial experts have delayed submitting to the court their statement on the bank's assets-to-liabilities ratio," the official told Reuters. He declined to specify the date.
Balkanbank sequestrators, appointed by the Bulgarian National Bank (BNB) to represent the bank while it is in receivership, were not immediately available for comment.

The BNB put Balkanbank in receivership on September 23 last year due to a capital-to-risk assets ratio of minus 37.85 percent as of August 31 and outstanding payments of 5.5 billion levs as of September 20.
The BNB opened a bankruptcy procedure against Balkanbank on October 31, saying it had ascertained Balkanbank's insolvency.

The court has previously delayed ruling on the case twice to give time for experts appointed by the court to prepare an independent report on the bank's assets-to-liabilities ratio at the time when the insolvency suit was filed.
The BNB opened bankruptcy procedures against 15 state and private banks or a third of Bulgaria's banks last year.
Four of them, Madan-based private Crystalbank, state-owned Mineralbank, Private Agricultural and Investment Bank and private Trade and Savings Bank, have been declared insolvent by the court so far.
Since the beginning of 1997 the BNB has sought insolvency for the private Capitalbank and has put in receivership the private International Bank for Investment and Development.

Under a memorandum of economic policies agreed with the International Monetary Fund in March, Bulgaria has pledged to adopt a new Bank Insolvency Act to speed up resolution of cases of banks which the BNB seeks to close down.
